Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 to 70 years.
- Holds an individual or joint savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- Agrees to join and allows the yearly premium to be auto-debited from that account.
- A person can be covered through only one account, even if they have several.
- In a joint account, each holder who meets the conditions can join by paying Rs 20 each.
Not eligible:
- Cover ends on reaching age 70 (age nearest birthday).
- Cover ends if the bank account is closed or does not have enough balance to pay the premium.
- Only accidents are covered; death by suicide is not covered, though murder is.
- If enrolled through more than one account, the extra premium is forfeited and cover is given through one account only.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Overview
A one-year accident insurance, renewed every year, for bank or post office account holders aged 18 to 70. It pays Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for a premium of Rs 20 a year taken automatically from the account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

User question:
मेरी उम्र 14 साल है। क्या मैं PMSBY में शामिल हो सकता हूँ?

Answer using only the retrieved context.
नहीं। PMSBY 18 से 70 वर्ष की उम्र के लोगों के लिए है, और 14 वर्ष 18 से कम है।

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a street vendor who sells goods or services to the public on streets, footpaths or other public places, from a temporary stall or by moving from place to place; seasonal or year-round, mobile or stationary.
- Must be an adult aged 18 years or above; there is no upper age limit.
- Vendors in cities and towns must hold a Certificate of Vending (CoV), Identity Card or Letter of Recommendation (LoR) issued by the Urban Local Body or Town Vending Committee.
- Vendors in census towns and peri-urban areas must have an LoR approved by the Block Development Officer (BDO).
- The 2nd and 3rd loans are given only after the previous loan is fully repaid.
- For the credit card only: must have repaid the 2nd loan and be eligible for or have taken the 3rd loan, and be aged 21 to 65 years.
Not eligible:
- People below 18 years of age.
- A lender may refuse the loan if the applicant has an existing loan classified as NPA or written off by any lender (a low credit score alone is not a reason to refuse).
- Manually issued LoRs are not valid; the LoR must be issued through the PM SVANidhi portal.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Overview
PM SVANidhi gives street vendors working capital loans without collateral in three steps: up to Rs 15,000, then Rs 25,000, then Rs 50,000. It also gives a 7% interest subsidy, cashback on digital payments and a RuPay credit card for vendors who repay well. New loans can be given until 31 March 2030 under the restructured scheme.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (with Department of Financial Services).

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Small or marginal farmer who owns cultivable land of up to 2 hectares as per state or UT land records.
- Aged 18 to 40 years at the time of joining.
- Name must appear in the state or UT land records as on 01.08.2019.
- Both men and women farmers can join, in any state or union territory.
- Must agree to pay a monthly contribution of Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on age at joining, until age 60.
Not eligible:
- Farmers already covered by another statutory social security scheme such as NPS, ESIC or an EPFO scheme.
- Farmers who have joined PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) or PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-Dhan (PM-LVM).
- Institutional landholders, and present or former holders of constitutional posts, Union or State ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, mayors of municipal corporations and district panchayat chairpersons.
- Serving or retired officers and employees of Central or State Government, PSUs and government autonomous bodies, and regular local body employees (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D are not excluded).
- Anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Practising professionals registered with a professional body: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Overview
A voluntary pension plan for small and marginal farmers (land up to 2 hectares) who join between ages 18 and 40. The farmer pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month, the Central Government adds the same amount, and from age 60 the farmer gets a guaranteed pension of at least Rs 3,000 a month.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare); pension fund managed by LIC.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Eligibility rules
- Open to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.
- The woman must be between 18 years 7 months and 55 years old when the child is born.
- She must belong to at least one listed disadvantaged group: SC or ST, disabled (40% or more), BPL ration card, NFSA ration card, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, e-Shram card, PM Kisan farmer, or MGNREGA job card.
- A net family income below Rs 8 lakh a year also counts as a qualifying group, even if none of the other groups apply.
- Pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi workers, Anganwadi helpers and ASHAs also qualify.
- The benefit covers the first child, and also the second child if the second child is a girl.
- For the second-child benefit, the pregnancy must be registered before delivery. The rules apply to births from 1 April 2022.
- The woman needs an Aadhaar number and a bank or post office account linked to Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Women with regular jobs in the Central Government, a State Government or a public sector undertaking cannot apply.
- Women who already get similar maternity benefits under another law cannot apply.
- There is no payment if the second child is a boy, and none for a third or later child.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Overview
PMMVY gives cash to pregnant women and new mothers from disadvantaged groups. They get Rs 5,000 in two instalments for the first child, and Rs 6,000 in one instalment if the second child is a girl. The money is paid straight into the woman's Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

User question:
My age is 61. Am I eligible for PMMVY?

Answer using only the retrieved context.
No. PMMVY is for people aged up to 55, and 61 is more than 55.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Parents' income from all sources must be no more than Rs 3,50,000 a year.
- You need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 7 exam to sit the selection test. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must study as a regular student in a government, government-aided or local body school.
- You must pass the state's selection test in Class 8 (Mental Ability Test and Scholastic Aptitude Test) with at least 40% marks in aggregate. The cut-off for SC/ST students is 32%.
- At the time of selection you need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 8 exam. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must be promoted from Class 8 to Class 9 to start receiving the scholarship.
- To continue, you must pass Class 9 and Class 11 in the first attempt, and you need at least 60% marks in Class 10 (5% lower for SC/ST students).
Not eligible:
- Students of Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.
- Students of residential schools run by Central or State Government institutions that provide boarding, lodging and education.
- Students of private schools.
- Diploma or certificate-level courses and studies abroad are not covered.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- A student can hold only one Central Government scholarship.
- The scholarship stops if there is a gap of one academic session, and once stopped it cannot be restarted.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Overview
A central scholarship of Rs 12,000 a year for bright students from low-income families studying in Class 9 to 12 in government, government-aided and local body schools. Students are chosen through a state-level test taken in Class 8, and 1,00,000 new scholarships are given every year.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy.

User question:
I earn Rs 467,765 a year. Am I eligible for NMMSS?

Answer using only the retrieved context.
No. NMMSS has an income limit of Rs 350,000 a year, and Rs 467,765 is more than that.

NPS Vatsalya — Eligibility rules
- The child must be below 18 years of age (17 or younger) when the account is opened.
- Open to Indian citizens under 18, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).
- A parent or legal guardian opens and runs the account in the child's name. The child is the only beneficiary.
- The minimum contribution is Rs 250 to open the account and at least Rs 250 in each financial year. There is no upper limit.
- For an NRI or OCI child, a bank account must be given (the minor's own or joint NRE/NRO account).
Not eligible:
- Anyone who has already turned 18 cannot open an NPS Vatsalya account. They can join the regular NPS instead.

NPS Vatsalya — Overview
A long-term savings and pension account under the National Pension System that a parent or guardian opens in the name of a child under 18, with as little as Rs 250 a year. When the child turns 18, they can move the money to a regular NPS account or take part of it out, and they can withdraw it all if the total is less than Rs 8 lakh.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services); regulated and administered by PFRDA.

Answer using only the retrieved context.
Yes, on age: NPS Vatsalya is for people aged up to 17, and 2 meets that. The other conditions in the rules must also be met.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Meant for rural poor households: at least one member of each identified poor household, preferably a woman, is brought into a Self Help Group.
- Poor households are identified by the community through the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process, and the list is vetted by the Gram Sabha; the BPL list alone is not used.
- SHGs usually have 10 to 20 members, mostly women; special SHGs in remote tribal or difficult areas, or of vulnerable people such as persons with disabilities, may have as few as 5 members.
- Groups of persons with disabilities, elderly people or transgender persons may include both men and women; other SHGs are women's groups.
- To get the Revolving Fund, an SHG should have existed for at least 3 to 6 months, follow the Panchasutras and not have received a Revolving Fund before.
- To get a bank loan, an SHG must have been active for at least 6 months as per its books of account and follow the Panchasutras: regular meetings, regular savings, regular inter-loaning, timely repayment and up-to-date books.
- The SHG must qualify under the grading norms fixed by NABARD.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- The poorest, single women, women-headed households, persons with disabilities, landless people and migrant labourers get special focus.
Not eligible:
- The mission is for rural areas; the interest subvention is only for women SHGs in rural areas.
- An SHG that has already received a Revolving Fund earlier cannot get it again.
- Interest subvention is given only while the SHG loan account stays in the standard (regularly repaid) category.
- A defunct SHG can get credit only after it is revived and stays active for at least 3 months.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Overview
DAY-NRLM brings at least one member of each poor rural household, preferably a woman, into a Self Help Group (SHG). It then supports these groups with a Revolving Fund of Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, community investment funds, bank loans without collateral, interest subvention and training. The mission is ongoing and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development through State Rural Livelihoods Missions.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Overview

Central government scheme. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (with Department of Financial Services).

- Has secured admission in a Quality Higher Educational Institution (QHEI) identified by the Ministry of Education.
- Admission should be on merit, for example through a recognised entrance exam or the merit quota.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Overview
Bank education loans with no collateral and no guarantor for students admitted to quality higher education institutions identified by the government. Loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh carry a 75% government credit guarantee, and students from families earning up to Rs 8 lakh a year can get 3% interest subvention. The Union Cabinet approved the scheme on 6 November 2024, and students apply on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education), with the Department of Financial Services.

- Practising professionals registered with a professional body: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Overview
A voluntary pension plan for small and marginal farmers (land up to 2 hectares) who join between ages 18 and 40. The farmer pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month, the Central Government adds the same amount, and from age 60 the farmer gets a guaranteed pension of at least Rs 3,000 a month.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Eligibility rules
- Open to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.
- The woman must be between 18 years 7 months and 55 years old when the child is born.
- She must belong to at least one listed disadvantaged group: SC or ST, disabled (40% or more), BPL ration card, NFSA ration card, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, e-Shram card, PM Kisan farmer, or MGNREGA job card.
- A net family income below Rs 8 lakh a year also counts as a qualifying group, even if none of the other groups apply.
- Pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi workers, Anganwadi helpers and ASHAs also qualify.
- The benefit covers the first child, and also the second child if the second child is a girl.
- For the second-child benefit, the pregnancy must be registered before delivery. The rules apply to births from 1 April 2022.
- The woman needs an Aadhaar number and a bank or post office account linked to Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Women with regular jobs in the Central Government, a State Government or a public sector undertaking cannot apply.
- Women who already get similar maternity benefits under another law cannot apply.
- There is no payment if the second child is a boy, and none for a third or later child.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Overview
PMMVY gives cash to pregnant women and new mothers from disadvantaged groups. They get Rs 5,000 in two instalments for the first child, and Rs 6,000 in one instalment if the second child is a girl. The money is paid straight into the woman's Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Overview
A monthly central pension for people aged 18 or above with severe (80% or more) or multiple disabilities from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

- You need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 7 exam to sit the selection test. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.

- Students of private schools.
- Diploma or certificate-level courses and studies abroad are not covered.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)

- The scholarship stops if there is a gap of one academic session, and once stopped it cannot be restarted.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Overview
A central scholarship of Rs 12,000 a year for bright students from low-income families studying in Class 9 to 12 in government, government-aided and local body schools. Students are chosen through a state-level test taken in Class 8, and 1,00,000 new scholarships are given every year.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy.

Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Central TB Division, National TB Elimination Programme).

- The child must be below 18 years of age (17 or younger) when the account is opened.
- Open to Indian citizens under 18, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).

Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services); regulated and administered by PFRDA.

Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Small or marginal farmer who owns cultivable land of up to 2 hectares as per state or UT land records.
- Aged 18 to 40 years at the time of joining.
- Name must appear in the state or UT land records as on 01.08.2019.
- Both men and women farmers can join, in any state or union territory.
- Must agree to pay a monthly contribution of Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on age at joining, until age 60.
Not eligible:
- Farmers already covered by another statutory social security scheme such as NPS, ESIC or an EPFO scheme.
- Farmers who have joined PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) or PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-Dhan (PM-LVM).
- Institutional landholders, and present or former holders of constitutional posts, Union or State ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, mayors of municipal corporations and district panchayat chairpersons.
- Serving or retired officers and employees of Central or State Government, PSUs and government autonomous bodies, and regular local body employees (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D are not excluded).
- Anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Practising professionals registered with a professional body: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Overview
A voluntary pension plan for small and marginal farmers (land up to 2 hectares) who join between ages 18 and 40. The farmer pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month, the Central Government adds the same amount, and from age 60 the farmer gets a guaranteed pension of at least Rs 3,000 a month.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare); pension fund managed by LIC.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Parents' income from all sources must be no more than Rs 3,50,000 a year.
- You need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 7 exam to sit the selection test. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must study as a regular student in a government, government-aided or local body school.
- You must pass the state's selection test in Class 8 (Mental Ability Test and Scholastic Aptitude Test) with at least 40% marks in aggregate. The cut-off for SC/ST students is 32%.
- At the time of selection you need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 8 exam. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must be promoted from Class 8 to Class 9 to start receiving the scholarship.
- To continue, you must pass Class 9 and Class 11 in the first attempt, and you need at least 60% marks in Class 10 (5% lower for SC/ST students).
Not eligible:
- Students of Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.
- Students of residential schools run by Central or State Government institutions that provide boarding, lodging and education.
- Students of private schools.
- Diploma or certificate-level courses and studies abroad are not covered.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- A student can hold only one Central Government scholarship.
- The scholarship stops if there is a gap of one academic session, and once stopped it cannot be restarted.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Overview
A central scholarship of Rs 12,000 a year for bright students from low-income families studying in Class 9 to 12 in government, government-aided and local body schools. Students are chosen through a state-level test taken in Class 8, and 1,00,000 new scholarships are given every year.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy.

- Must be a widow.

- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).

Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Overview
A monthly central pension for widows aged 40 or above from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top, so the total paid varies by state.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

Central government scheme. Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education), with the Department of Financial Services.

- Your family must own cultivable land, and the names must be entered in the state or UT land records.
- For this scheme a farmer family means husband, wife and minor children.
- There is no upper limit on land size; the original 2-hectare cap was dropped when the scheme was opened to all landholding farmer families.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Overview
Gives Rs 6,000 a year, paid as three instalments of Rs 2,000, directly into the bank accounts of farmer families who own cultivable land. Families with a better-off member, such as income tax payers, government employees or pensioners getting Rs 10,000 or more a month, are left out.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare).

Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a widow.
- Aged 40 years or above.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If her name is missing from the BPL list but she is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave her out and to check and establish her eligibility.
- A widow living with AIDS can be covered even if her household is not BPL, provided none of the exclusions below apply to her.
Not eligible:
- Widows from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme, except the special case of widows living with AIDS.
- A widow living with AIDS who is not BPL is still excluded if she has a government job, owns 5 acres or more of land, or owns a four-wheeler for her own use.
- The pension can be stopped after the yearly verification if the household is no longer BPL or if she has moved away; it can be restored on appeal if she becomes eligible again.

Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Overview
A monthly central pension for widows aged 40 or above from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top, so the total paid varies by state.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Eligibility rules
- You must live in a rural area (a village).
- Your household has no house, or lives in a kutcha house.
- Your present house has no more than 2 rooms.
- No member of your household owns a pucca house.
- Families are chosen from the SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data and the Awaas+ survey lists, and the Gram Sabha checks the list.
- These families get top priority (automatic inclusion): those with no shelter, destitute families living on alms, manual scavengers, Primitive Tribal Group families and legally freed bonded labourers.
Not eligible:
- Anyone in the household owns a motorised three-wheeler or four-wheeler, or mechanised three- or four-wheeler farm equipment.
- Anyone in the household has a Kisan Credit Card with a limit of Rs 50,000 or more.
- Any household member is a government employee, or the household runs a non-farm business registered with the government.
- Any household member earns more than Rs 15,000 a month.
- Anyone in the household pays income tax or professional tax.
- The household owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Overview
PMAY-G gives money to poor rural families who have no house or live in a kutcha house so they can build a pucca house. The grant is Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hill, north-eastern and difficult areas. The scheme is still running: its second phase adds 2 crore more houses, and the overall target is 4.95 crore houses by March 2029.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Rural Development).

Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) — Eligibility rules
- Any Indian citizen who is eligible to open an ordinary bank account can open a basic savings account under the scheme.
- The account is meant for people who do not already have a bank account.
- Since 2018 the scheme aims to reach every adult without a bank account, not just one account per household.

Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) — Overview
A national mission that helps people with no bank account open a basic savings account with no minimum balance. Account holders get a free RuPay debit card with accident insurance, and eligible holders can get an overdraft of up to Rs 10,000. The scheme started on 28 August 2014 and is still open.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

NPS Vatsalya — Eligibility rules
- The child must be below 18 years of age (17 or younger) when the account is opened.
- Open to Indian citizens under 18, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).
- A parent or legal guardian opens and runs the account in the child's name. The child is the only beneficiary.
- The minimum contribution is Rs 250 to open the account and at least Rs 250 in each financial year. There is no upper limit.
- For an NRI or OCI child, a bank account must be given (the minor's own or joint NRE/NRO account).
Not eligible:
- Anyone who has already turned 18 cannot open an NPS Vatsalya account. They can join the regular NPS instead.

NPS Vatsalya — Overview
A long-term savings and pension account under the National Pension System that a parent or guardian opens in the name of a child under 18, with as little as Rs 250 a year. When the child turns 18, they can move the money to a regular NPS account or take part of it out, and they can withdraw it all if the total is less than Rs 8 lakh.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services); regulated and administered by PFRDA.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Small or marginal farmer who owns cultivable land of up to 2 hectares as per state or UT land records.
- Aged 18 to 40 years at the time of joining.
- Name must appear in the state or UT land records as on 01.08.2019.
- Both men and women farmers can join, in any state or union territory.
- Must agree to pay a monthly contribution of Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on age at joining, until age 60.
Not eligible:
- Farmers already covered by another statutory social security scheme such as NPS, ESIC or an EPFO scheme.
- Farmers who have joined PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) or PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-Dhan (PM-LVM).
- Institutional landholders, and present or former holders of constitutional posts, Union or State ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, mayors of municipal corporations and district panchayat chairpersons.
- Serving or retired officers and employees of Central or State Government, PSUs and government autonomous bodies, and regular local body employees (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D are not excluded).
- Anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Practising professionals registered with a professional body: doctors, engineers, lawyers, chartered accountants and architects.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Overview
A voluntary pension plan for small and marginal farmers (land up to 2 hectares) who join between ages 18 and 40. The farmer pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month, the Central Government adds the same amount, and from age 60 the farmer gets a guaranteed pension of at least Rs 3,000 a month.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare); pension fund managed by LIC.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Eligibility rules
- Has secured admission in a Quality Higher Educational Institution (QHEI) identified by the Ministry of Education.
- Admission should be on merit, for example through a recognised entrance exam or the merit quota.
- To get the 3% interest subvention, annual family income must be Rs 8 lakh or less, and the subvention applies to loans up to Rs 10 lakh.
- The 3% interest subvention is limited to 1 lakh students a year, chosen in this order of preference: admission to a government institution, then technical/professional courses, then students who passed Class 12 or Class 10 from a government school, then those who passed Class 12 from a rural school, then girl students.
- Aadhaar is required to get the scheme's benefits, including the loan, interest subvention and credit guarantee.
Not eligible:
- Education loans for admissions under management quota are not eligible.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Overview
Bank education loans with no collateral and no guarantor for students admitted to quality higher education institutions identified by the government. Loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh carry a 75% government credit guarantee, and students from families earning up to Rs 8 lakh a year can get 3% interest subvention. The Union Cabinet approved the scheme on 6 November 2024, and students apply on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education), with the Department of Financial Services.

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Overview
A monthly central pension for people aged 18 or above with severe (80% or more) or multiple disabilities from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Eligibility rules
- You must be a TB (tuberculosis) patient who is notified (registered) on the Ni-kshay portal.
- Patients treated in the private sector qualify too, as long as they are notified on Ni-kshay.
- New, previously treated and drug-resistant TB patients are all covered.

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Overview
Gives every TB patient registered (notified) on the Ni-kshay portal money every month for nutritious food for the whole time they are on TB treatment, paid by direct bank transfer. The amount was raised from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 per month in late 2024.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Central TB Division, National TB Elimination Programme).

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 to 70 years.
- Holds an individual or joint savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- Agrees to join and allows the yearly premium to be auto-debited from that account.
- A person can be covered through only one account, even if they have several.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Overview
A one-year accident insurance, renewed every year, for bank or post office account holders aged 18 to 70. It pays Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for a premium of Rs 20 a year taken automatically from the account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a widow.
- Aged 40 years or above.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If her name is missing from the BPL list but she is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave her out and to check and establish her eligibility.
- A widow living with AIDS can be covered even if her household is not BPL, provided none of the exclusions below apply to her.
Not eligible:
- Widows from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme, except the special case of widows living with AIDS.
- A widow living with AIDS who is not BPL is still excluded if she has a government job, owns 5 acres or more of land, or owns a four-wheeler for her own use.
- The pension can be stopped after the yearly verification if the household is no longer BPL or if she has moved away; it can be restored on appeal if she becomes eligible again.

Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) — Overview
A monthly central pension for widows aged 40 or above from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top, so the total paid varies by state.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Eligibility rules
- Open to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.
- The woman must be between 18 years 7 months and 55 years old when the child is born.
- She must belong to at least one listed disadvantaged group: SC or ST, disabled (40% or more), BPL ration card, NFSA ration card, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, e-Shram card, PM Kisan farmer, or MGNREGA job card.
- A net family income below Rs 8 lakh a year also counts as a qualifying group, even if none of the other groups apply.
- Pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi workers, Anganwadi helpers and ASHAs also qualify.
- The benefit covers the first child, and also the second child if the second child is a girl.
- For the second-child benefit, the pregnancy must be registered before delivery. The rules apply to births from 1 April 2022.
- The woman needs an Aadhaar number and a bank or post office account linked to Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Women with regular jobs in the Central Government, a State Government or a public sector undertaking cannot apply.
- Women who already get similar maternity benefits under another law cannot apply.
- There is no payment if the second child is a boy, and none for a third or later child.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Overview
PMMVY gives cash to pregnant women and new mothers from disadvantaged groups. They get Rs 5,000 in two instalments for the first child, and Rs 6,000 in one instalment if the second child is a girl. The money is paid straight into the woman's Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If the name is missing from the BPL list but the person is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave them out and to check and establish eligibility.
Not eligible:
- People from households that are not BPL are not covered by the central scheme.
- A certified disability below 80% does not meet the central scheme's severity level, unless the person has multiple disabilities; some states run their own disability pensions with different rules.
- The pension can be stopped after the yearly verification if the household is no longer BPL or the person has moved away; it can be restored on appeal if they become eligible again.

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Overview
A monthly central pension for people aged 18 or above with severe (80% or more) or multiple disabilities from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development, Department of Rural Development (National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP).

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Eligibility rules
- You must live in a rural area (a village).
- Your household has no house, or lives in a kutcha house.
- Your present house has no more than 2 rooms.
- No member of your household owns a pucca house.
- Families are chosen from the SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data and the Awaas+ survey lists, and the Gram Sabha checks the list.
- These families get top priority (automatic inclusion): those with no shelter, destitute families living on alms, manual scavengers, Primitive Tribal Group families and legally freed bonded labourers.
Not eligible:
- Anyone in the household owns a motorised three-wheeler or four-wheeler, or mechanised three- or four-wheeler farm equipment.
- Anyone in the household has a Kisan Credit Card with a limit of Rs 50,000 or more.
- Any household member is a government employee, or the household runs a non-farm business registered with the government.
- Any household member earns more than Rs 15,000 a month.
- Anyone in the household pays income tax or professional tax.
- The household owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Overview
PMAY-G gives money to poor rural families who have no house or live in a kutcha house so they can build a pucca house. The grant is Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hill, north-eastern and difficult areas. The scheme is still running: its second phase adds 2 crore more houses, and the overall target is 4.95 crore houses by March 2029.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Rural Development).

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Meant for rural poor households: at least one member of each identified poor household, preferably a woman, is brought into a Self Help Group.
- Poor households are identified by the community through the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process, and the list is vetted by the Gram Sabha; the BPL list alone is not used.
- SHGs usually have 10 to 20 members, mostly women; special SHGs in remote tribal or difficult areas, or of vulnerable people such as persons with disabilities, may have as few as 5 members.
- Groups of persons with disabilities, elderly people or transgender persons may include both men and women; other SHGs are women's groups.
- To get the Revolving Fund, an SHG should have existed for at least 3 to 6 months, follow the Panchasutras and not have received a Revolving Fund before.
- To get a bank loan, an SHG must have been active for at least 6 months as per its books of account and follow the Panchasutras: regular meetings, regular savings, regular inter-loaning, timely repayment and up-to-date books.
- The SHG must qualify under the grading norms fixed by NABARD.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- The poorest, single women, women-headed households, persons with disabilities, landless people and migrant labourers get special focus.
Not eligible:
- The mission is for rural areas; the interest subvention is only for women SHGs in rural areas.
- An SHG that has already received a Revolving Fund earlier cannot get it again.
- Interest subvention is given only while the SHG loan account stays in the standard (regularly repaid) category.
- A defunct SHG can get credit only after it is revived and stays active for at least 3 months.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Overview
DAY-NRLM brings at least one member of each poor rural household, preferably a woman, into a Self Help Group (SHG). It then supports these groups with a Revolving Fund of Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, community investment funds, bank loans without collateral, interest subvention and training. The mission is ongoing and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development through State Rural Livelihoods Missions.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.
